comparison: Both evaluate the core threshold concept (C38-C44, C39-C44). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED despite R²=0.42 variability, noting the large sample size and consistency. This represents the most significant disagreement.

Partial overlap on C6-C7. OpenEval rates the spatial threshold evidence as SUPPORTED based on statistical correlations and large sample size. Peer reviewers acknowledge the correlation but express UNCERTAINTY about the threshold interpretation, noting that some astrocytes deviate from the proposed threshold pattern. OpenEval focuses on population-level statistics while peer reviewers emphasize individual cell variability.

Both address C26-C31 describing distribution of responses and correlations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with emphasis on statistical significance. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging these as solid descriptive findings without challenge. This represents strong agreement on the observational data.

Perfect claim overlap (C8, C57-C61, C70-C72) on IP3R2 knockout experiments. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes smaller sample size in knockout mice. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, arguing the claim of 'necessity' is too strong because non-zero somatic activity persists in IP3R2-/- mice. Both acknowledge the strong effect but disagree on whether 'necessity' is justified.

Perfect claim overlap (C9, C62-C67, C74) on functional impact via SICs. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on strong correlation (R²=0.95) and threshold consistency. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging correlation but questioning whether the data establish causation or functional impact of the threshold per se. Disagreement centers on inferential leap from correlation to functional consequence.

Perfect claim overlap (C32-C37) on temporal analysis and centripetal propagation. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and internal consistency. Peer reviewers do not challenge these temporal measurements. This represents strong agreement on the kinetic data.

High overlap (C45-C52, C38) on spatiotemporal analysis and GLM findings. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistics and GLM identification of percent area as primary driver. Peer reviewers request more statistical details but do not dispute findings. Agreement on the analytical approach and results.

High overlap (C53-C56, C92) on bidirectional propagation and centripetal-to-centrifugal switch. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong correlations but acknowledges C56 extends beyond direct measurement. Peer reviewers do not challenge these propagation findings. Agreement on this novel observation.

Overlap on C93, C96 regarding methodological tools. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing the tool's validation through prior publications and public availability. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, highlighting that methodological limitations remain 'important caveats' including concerns about spatial resolution and physiological monitoring adequacy. Disagreement on whether methods are sufficiently robust.

Overlap on C95 regarding experimental limitations. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval acknowledges anesthesia as a limitation partially addressed by slice experiments. Peer reviewers emphasize physiological monitoring concerns (O2/CO2 control) as 'considerable caveats.' Agreement that limitations exist, with peer reviewers expressing stronger concern about their impact.

Minimal overlap on C92 regarding surge mechanism. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for mechanistic details about directional switch. Peer reviewers include C92 in their SUPPORTED evaluation of propagation patterns. Agreement on this aspect of the findings.

Minimal overlap on C41 regarding threshold independence from stimulus parameters. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as part of conceptual framework.
